notes: Each strain carries a single copy of the chymosin gene, inserted at the same locus (niaD), confirmed by Southern blot, so strains are comparable on copy number and integration site. The disruptant also had reduced extracellular protease activity in culture medium: total protease activity down (Fig. 5A), and the specific tripeptidyl peptidase activity attributed to AoSedD down ~40% (per Discussion; Fig. 5B). This supports the explanation that more chymosin survived because less was being degraded. Fig. 5 names its control strain inconsistently - NSlD1 in the plot key, NSPlD1 in the caption text; not resolved by the paper. The disruptant grew normally, with no reported growth or morphological defects (Results, AosedD disruption section).
